short: Metal-Organic Framework Cathodes Based on a Vanadium Hexacya
title: Metal-Organic Framework Cathodes Based on a Vanadium Hexacyanoferrate Prussian Blue Analogue for High-Performance Aqueous Rechargeable Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Aqueous rechargeable batteries need cathodes above the ~50-65 mAh/g delivered by earlier PBAs. A V/Fe PBA with redox-active V and Fe sites could exceed Fe-only PBA capacity by multi-electron redox.
states.detail: Absorbed: h1 (HYP/need), h2 (HYP/hypothesis), d1 (DES/base_system), d2 (DES/variable_sweep), d3 (DES/method), p1 (PRC/synthesis), p2 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Crystallinity rises (amorphous fraction falls): simple mixing < co-precipitation w/o HCl < w/ HCl. Charge is compensated by both V (V3+ to V4+ to V5+) and Fe (Fe2+ to Fe3+) valence changes.
states.detail: Absorbed: s3 (STR/phase/fraction), s6 (STR/chemistry/composition), s8 (STR/chemistry/composition). Premises: K-edge or pre-edge energy rises roughly linearly with transition-metal valence

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Residual amorphous region around crystallites acts as an extra interface (film resistance) hindering the electrochemical process. Electrochemical utilization and capacity retention increase with crystallinity.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), r1 (PRP/value), m2 (MEC/identification), r2 (PRP/value), r4 (PRP/value). Premises: Electrodeposited V/Fe PBA films show three couples: V(III)/V(IV)O, Fe(II)/Fe(III), V(IV)/V(V)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Initial discharge capacity 91 mAh/g at 110 mA/g, above earlier aqueous PBAs (50-65 mAh/g). Capacity fades from 91 to ~55 mAh/g over 250 cycles, mostly in early cycles, at ~100% coulombic efficiency
states.detail: Absorbed: f1 (PRF/service_capability), f3 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Earlier aqueous PBAs: Cu/Fe ~55, Ni/Fe ~50-60, Cu/Ni/Fe 50-65 mAh/g; oxides/phosphates 60-80

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Well-crystallized V/Fe PBA gives high aqueous capacity through V and Fe multi-redox; fading traces to V-site dissolution raising Rct

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: Fe K-edge shifts to higher energy as charge potential rises 0.45 to 1.15 V, between FeO and Fe2O3. V K pre-edge peak shifts to higher energy with potential, lying between V2O3/VO2 and V2O5 references.
nodes.solves: Charge is compensated by both V (V3+ to V4+ to V5+) and Fe (Fe2+ to Fe3+) valence changes
nodes.op: compare across conditions, compare with reference value, read trend, replot derived series
nodes.note: Fe2+ line ~7120.4, Fe3+ line ~7126.3 eV; points ~7124.3 to ~7125.9 eV. Text concedes formal oxidation states cannot be fixed; plotted Fe position argues for partial Fe2+/Fe3+ conversion only
nodes.detail: o16: Fe K-edge shifts to higher energy as charge potential rises 0.45 to 1.15 V, between FeO and Fe2O3; o17: V K pre-edge peak shifts to higher energy with potential, lying between V2O3/VO2 and V2O5 references; o18: Fe edge (~7124.3 to 7125.9 eV) and V pre-edge (~5469.75 to 5470.5 eV) rise monotonically with normalized charge; o19: At zero charge Fe edge sits ~2/3 toward the Fe3+ line; shift only ~1.6 of ~5.9 eV span; V between V3+ and V5+

nodes.title: ECHEM:EIS, F5

nodes.op: compare across conditions, correlate across series, read trend
nodes.note: high-frequency magnification is in Fig. S6A (not in packet); Rct growth rests on the fit rise continues to 150 cycles, later than the capacity drop in F2a; error bars overlap after 60 cycles
